cards.front: Recall a key point about The Skeletal System
cards.back: The adult human skeleton is made up of 206 bones . At birth, humans have around 270 bones, but many fuse together as the body grows.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Skeletal System
cards.back: The pectoral girdle (shoulder) and pelvic girdle (hip) are part of the appendicular skeleton, not the axial. A common mistake is thinking the pelvis belongs to the axial skeleton because it's in the centre of the body.

cards.front: What should you know about you must know all five functions?
cards.back: Support, Protection, Movement, Mineral Storage, Blood Cell Production.

cards.front: What should you know about the vertebral column?
cards.back: consists of 33 vertebrae stacked on top of each other, separated by intervertebral discs that act as shock absorbers.

cards.front: What should you know about long bone structure?
cards.back: A long bone has an outer layer of compact bone (dense and strong) and an inner layer of spongy bone (light and shock-absorbing). The shaft is called the diaphysis and the ends are called epiphyses .

cards.front: What does Number of bones mean?

cards.back: Central axis of the body (e.g. Limbs and limb attachments)
Skull, vertebral column, ribcage, sternum (e.g. Arms, legs, pectoral girdle, pelvic girdle)
Protection of vital organs, support of upright posture (e.g. Movement and locomotion)
Cranium (8 bones), vertebrae (33), ribs (24), sternum (1) (e.g. Humerus, radius, ulna, femur, tibia, fibula, scapula, clavicle, pelvis)
Longer than they are wide; shaft with two ends (e.g. Act as levers for movement; contain red marrow in ends)
Roughly cube-shaped; spongy inside (e.g. Provide stability and some movement; absorb shock)
Thin, flattened and often curved (e.g. Protection of organs; large area for muscle attachment)
Do not fit into other categories; complex shapes (e.g. Various - protection, support, muscle attachment)
